Long searches in the background

Source: vignettes/background-searches.qmd 
library(BLASTr)

Searching in the background

Large searches (thousands of sequences against core_nt) can take hours. With background = TRUE, parallel_blast() starts the search in a separate process and returns a job at once, so the R session stays free. The job keeps its batches and results in a directory (job_dir; by default a new directory in the BLASTr cache), so it goes on even if the R session ends, and can be opened again from another session.

job <- parallel_blast(
  query_seqs = seqs,
  db_path = "~/blast_databases/core_nt_2026-11-17/core_nt",
  total_cores = 32,
  background = TRUE,
  job_dir = "~/blast_jobs/run_01" # a fixed place, to find it again
)

blast_job_status(job) # batches done, progress and estimated time left

To get the results, blast_job_result() waits for the end (with a progress bar in interactive sessions) and returns the same table as parallel_blast(); with wait = FALSE it returns NULL while the job is not finished.

blast_results <- blast_job_result(job)

# later, or in another R session
job <- blast_job("~/blast_jobs/run_01")
blast_job_status(job)
blast_results <- blast_job_result(job, wait = FALSE)

blast_job_cancel() stops a job. If the process running it stopped (for example, the machine was restarted), blast_job_status() reports the job as stopped and blast_job_resume() restarts it: the batches already finished are kept and only the others are searched again.

blast_job_cancel(job)
blast_job_resume("~/blast_jobs/run_01")
